questions.s: The Eiffel Tower is in which city?
questions.e: The iron tower was built for the 1889 World's Fair in Paris. It is a landmark of France.

questions.s: The first FIFA World Cup was held in 1930 in
questions.e: Uruguay hosted and won the first tournament. Italy and England hosted later editions.

questions.s: The Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (founded 1969) has its headquarters in
questions.e: The OIC is based in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, and was formed after the 1969 Rabat summit. Riyadh is the Saudi capital but not the OIC seat.

questions.s: Who was the first Pakistani to win a Nobel Prize?
questions.e: Abdus Salam shared the 1979 Nobel Prize in Physics for work on electroweak unification. Malala won the Peace Prize in 2014, much later.

questions.s: Which Yugoslav leader was one of the founders of the Non-Aligned Movement?
questions.e: Tito, with Nehru and Nasser, is counted among the founders. Only Tito led Yugoslavia, while the others led India and Egypt, and Sukarno led Indonesia.

questions.s: The Protestant Reformation began in 1517 when Martin Luther challenged the Church in
questions.e: Luther, a German monk, posted his Ninety-five Theses at Wittenberg. England's break with Rome came later under Henry VIII.

questions.s: Who was the first emperor of ancient Rome?
questions.e: Augustus, born Octavian, became the first emperor in 27 BC. Julius Caesar was a dictator who was killed before the empire began.

questions.s: The Ramsar Convention is an international treaty for the conservation of
questions.e: Signed in 1971 in the Iranian city of Ramsar, it protects wetlands of international importance, especially for waterfowl.

questions.s: Which war was fought between the Allied Powers and the Central Powers?
questions.e: Britain, France and Russia, later joined by the USA, fought Germany, Austria-Hungary and the Ottoman Empire. The Second World War had different alignments.

questions.s: The Mughal emperor who built the Taj Mahal was
questions.e: Shah Jahan built it at Agra in memory of Mumtaz Mahal. Akbar was his grandfather.

questions.s: Who was President of the United States during the American Civil War?
questions.e: Lincoln led the Union from 1861 and issued the Emancipation Proclamation. Washington was president in the 1790s, long before.

questions.s: Constantinople fell to the Ottomans in 1453 under which sultan?
questions.e: Mehmed II, called the Conqueror, took the Byzantine capital and made it the Ottoman capital. Suleiman ruled much later, in the 1500s.

questions.s: Which Muslim scholar is regarded as the founder of algebra and gave his name to the word 'algorithm'?
questions.e: Al-Khwarizmi wrote the book on al-jabr in Baghdad in the ninth century. Al-Biruni is known for science and geography.

questions.s: Which UN agency focuses on the welfare of children?
questions.e: UNICEF works for children's health, nutrition and education. UNHCR deals with refugees, and UNESCO with education, science and culture.

questions.s: The First Battle of Panipat in 1526 led to the founding of the
questions.e: Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi and laid the foundation of Mughal rule. The Delhi Sultanate had begun centuries earlier, in 1206.

questions.s: The Geneva Conventions mainly deal with
o: treatment of the wounded and prisoners in war
questions.e: The conventions set rules for protecting the sick, wounded, prisoners of war and civilians in armed conflict. Trade and nuclear tests are covered by other agreements.

questions.s: Democracy was first practised in the ancient Greek city-state of
questions.e: Athenian citizens voted directly on laws in an assembly. Sparta was known for a military state instead.

questions.s: In which year did the Second World War end?
questions.e: Germany surrendered in May 1945 and Japan in August–September 1945. 1947 is when British India was partitioned.

questions.s: The treaty of Maastricht, signed in 1992, laid the basis of the
questions.e: It created the European Union and paved the way for a single currency. NATO dates from 1949.

questions.s: Which explorer reached the Americas in 1492 on a voyage from Spain?
questions.e: Columbus sailed west under the Spanish crown and landed in the Caribbean. Vasco da Gama sailed around Africa to India, not to the Americas.

questions.s: In which year was the United Nations founded?
questions.e: The UN came into being in October 1945, after the Second World War, when its Charter took effect. 1919 is associated with the League of Nations, its failed predecessor.

questions.s: Marco Polo, who travelled to China and wrote about it, came from
questions.e: Marco Polo was a Venetian merchant who reached the court of Kublai Khan. Ibn Battuta, by contrast, was from Morocco.

questions.s: The Ottoman sultanate was abolished in 1922, and Turkey became a republic in
questions.e: Mustafa Kemal Ataturk declared the republic in October 1923. The Ottoman Empire had joined the First World War in 1914.

questions.s: The Industrial Revolution began in which country?
questions.e: Textile mills, coal and the steam engine transformed Britain from the later 1700s. Other countries industrialised later and borrowed British methods.

questions.s: In which year was the Universal Declaration of Human Rights adopted by the UN General Assembly?
questions.e: The Declaration was adopted in December 1948. 1945 is the year of the UN's founding, so it is the tempting wrong choice.

questions.s: Which ancient people of Mesopotamia invented cuneiform writing?
questions.e: The Sumerians pressed wedge-shaped marks into clay tablets around 3000 BC. Egyptians used hieroglyphs, and the Phoenicians gave the world an alphabet.

questions.s: The assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand in 1914 took place in
questions.e: The heir to the Austro-Hungarian throne was shot in Sarajevo, which triggered the chain of events leading to the First World War.

questions.s: The Renaissance, a revival of art and learning, began in
questions.e: The movement began in Italian cities such as Florence in the 1300s. Printing later helped spread it across Europe.

questions.s: The ship RMS Titanic sank on its first voyage in
questions.e: The liner hit an iceberg in the North Atlantic in April 1912. 1914 is the start of the First World War.

questions.s: The International Court of Justice, the main judicial organ of the UN, sits in
questions.e: The ICJ is located in the Peace Palace at The Hague in the Netherlands. It settles disputes between states, unlike the International Criminal Court, which tries individuals.

questions.s: How many permanent members does the UN Security Council have?
questions.e: The permanent members are China, France, Russia, the United Kingdom and the United States. Ten is the number of elected, non-permanent members, so it is a common confusion.

questions.s: Who was the first human to walk on the Moon?
questions.e: Armstrong stepped onto the Moon in July 1969 during Apollo 11, with Aldrin following. Gagarin was the first human in space, not on the Moon.

questions.s: The American Declaration of Independence was adopted in
questions.e: The thirteen colonies declared independence from Britain on 4 July 1776. 1865 marks the end of the American Civil War.

questions.s: United Nations peacekeeping soldiers are recognised by their
questions.e: UN peacekeepers wear light-blue helmets or berets, matching the UN flag colour. White vehicles are also used, but the helmets are the distinctive mark.

questions.s: Mahatma Gandhi led the famous Salt March in
questions.e: Gandhi walked to Dandi on the Gujarat coast in 1930 to protest against the salt tax. 1942 is the year of the Quit India movement.

questions.s: Which city was divided by a wall from 1961 until 1989?
questions.e: The Berlin Wall separated East and West Berlin during the Cold War and was opened in November 1989. The other cities were not split by such a wall.

questions.s: The Bandung Conference of 1955, a meeting of Asian and African states, was held in
questions.e: Bandung is in Java, Indonesia. The meeting led towards the Non-Aligned Movement. Pakistan attended but did not host it.

questions.s: Who made the first successful powered aeroplane flight in 1903?
questions.e: Orville and Wilbur Wright flew at Kitty Hawk, North Carolina. The Montgolfiers built hot-air balloons in 1783.

questions.s: Which general crossed the Alps with elephants to attack Rome in the Second Punic War?
questions.e: Hannibal of Carthage invaded Italy in 218 BC. Scipio later defeated him at Zama in North Africa.

questions.s: Which Portuguese navigator reached India by sea in 1498?
questions.e: Da Gama sailed around the Cape of Good Hope and reached Calicut. Dias had earlier rounded the Cape but turned back before India.

questions.s: The Rosetta Stone helped scholars decipher which ancient writing?
questions.e: The stone carries the same text in three scripts, which let Champollion decode hieroglyphs in the 1820s. The Indus script remains undeciphered.

questions.s: Which American leader is associated with the 'I have a dream' speech of 1963?
questions.e: King gave it during the March on Washington for civil rights. Lincoln lived a century earlier.

questions.s: The Book of Optics was written by
questions.e: Ibn al-Haytham (Alhazen) explained vision by light entering the eye. Ibn Sina wrote on medicine.

questions.s: In the UN General Assembly, how many votes does each member state have?
questions.e: Each state has a single vote, big or small. Veto power exists only in the Security Council, for the five permanent members.

questions.s: The International Red Cross movement was inspired by which Swiss businessman?
questions.e: Dunant was moved by the suffering after the Battle of Solferino in 1859 and later helped found the Red Cross. Nobel founded the prizes that bear his name.

questions.s: The International Monetary Fund and the World Bank have their headquarters in
questions.e: Both institutions were created at the Bretton Woods conference in 1944 and are based in Washington, D.C. New York is the seat of the UN itself.

questions.s: The World Trade Organization began operating in
questions.e: The WTO replaced the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT) on 1 January 1995. Its seat is in Geneva.

questions.s: The Interpol, the international police cooperation organisation, has its headquarters in
questions.e: The headquarters are in Lyon, France. Many people guess Geneva or Brussels because other bodies are there.

questions.s: In which year was the Soviet Union dissolved?
questions.e: The USSR ended in December 1991, splitting into fifteen independent states. 1989 saw the fall of the Berlin Wall, which came earlier.

questions.s: Charles Darwin published On the Origin of Species in
questions.e: The book set out evolution by natural selection. 1809 is the year of Darwin's birth, a common mix-up.

questions.s: Which Swedish chemist, inventor of dynamite, founded the Nobel Prizes?
questions.e: Alfred Nobel left his fortune in his will to fund the prizes, first awarded in 1901. Celsius and Linnaeus were also Swedish scientists but not the founders.

questions.s: The Cold War was mainly a rivalry between which two superpowers?
questions.e: After 1945 the United States and the Soviet Union competed without fighting each other directly. The other pairs were wartime opponents or allies, not Cold War blocs.

questions.s: Who was the first President of the United States?
questions.e: Washington led the country from 1789 to 1797. Lincoln was the sixteenth president.

questions.s: Alexander the Great fought King Porus at the Battle of the Hydaspes in the year
questions.e: Alexander defeated Porus on the Jhelum river in 326 BC, which lies in present-day Punjab. 480 BC is the date of the Greek battles with Persia at Thermopylae.

questions.s: Which Scottish engineer greatly improved the steam engine in the 1700s?
questions.e: Watt's separate condenser made steam engines far more efficient. Stephenson is remembered for the steam locomotive and railways.

questions.s: Ibn Sina (Avicenna) wrote the medical encyclopedia known as
questions.e: His Canon was used in European universities for centuries. The Book of Optics is by Ibn al-Haytham, and the Muqaddimah by Ibn Khaldun.

questions.s: The Marshall Plan of 1948 offered American aid to
questions.e: The plan helped western European economies recover after the Second World War and limit Soviet influence. It did not target Africa or Asia.

questions.s: ASEAN, the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, has its secretariat in which city?
questions.e: The ASEAN Secretariat is in Jakarta, Indonesia. Bangkok is where the association was founded in 1967, which makes it a tempting choice.

questions.s: Which country is NOT a permanent member of the UN Security Council?
questions.e: The five permanent members are China, France, Russia, the UK and the USA. Germany is a major economy but holds no permanent seat.

questions.s: Who is credited with introducing movable-type printing to Europe around 1450?
questions.e: Gutenberg of Mainz printed the famous Bible with movable metal type. Caxton later brought printing to England.

questions.s: The Montreal Protocol of 1987 is an agreement to protect the
questions.e: Countries agreed to phase out chemicals such as CFCs that damage the ozone layer. Whale protection falls under a different convention.

questions.s: The ancient Olympic Games were first held in
questions.e: They were held at Olympia in Greece to honour Zeus. The modern games were revived in Athens in 1896.

questions.s: In which city is the headquarters of UNESCO?
questions.e: UNESCO, which works on education, science and culture, is headquartered in Paris. Rome hosts the FAO instead.

questions.s: Nelson Mandela was imprisoned for opposing the system of
questions.e: Apartheid was South Africa's legal system of racial segregation. Mandela spent 27 years in prison and became president in 1994.

questions.s: The Suez Canal, linking the Mediterranean and the Red Sea, was opened in
questions.e: The canal opened under a French company led by Ferdinand de Lesseps. 1914 is the year the Panama Canal opened.

questions.s: In which year did the Second World War begin in Europe?
questions.e: Germany invaded Poland in September 1939. 1945 is the year the war ended, and 1941 is when the United States entered it.

questions.s: In which Swiss city is the headquarters of the World Health Organization?
questions.e: The WHO is based in Geneva, as are the ILO and the International Red Cross. Bern is the Swiss capital but does not house the WHO.

questions.s: The Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) has its headquarters in
questions.e: The FAO is based in Rome and works to fight hunger. Geneva hosts agencies such as the WHO and ILO.

questions.s: The Russian Revolution that brought the Bolsheviks to power took place in
questions.e: The Bolsheviks under Lenin took power in October (November, new style) 1917. 1905 was an earlier uprising that failed to topple the Tsar.

questions.s: The ancient Silk Road mainly linked
questions.e: This network of land routes carried silk, spices and ideas between China and the Mediterranean. Australia and South America were outside it.

questions.s: The People's Republic of China was proclaimed by Mao Zedong in
questions.e: Mao announced it in Beijing in October 1949 after the communist victory in the civil war. 1911 is the year the Qing dynasty fell.

questions.s: The Battle of Plassey in 1757 helped establish the power of the
questions.e: Robert Clive defeated Nawab Siraj ud-Daulah of Bengal, opening the way for Company rule. The French were challenged but not established in this battle.

questions.s: The capital of the Umayyad caliphate was
questions.e: Mu'awiya made Damascus the centre of the Umayyads from 661. Baghdad belonged to the next dynasty, the Abbasids.

questions.s: The Cuban Missile Crisis, a tense Cold War standoff, occurred in
questions.e: In October 1962 the USA and USSR came close to war over Soviet missiles in Cuba.

questions.s: Napoleon Bonaparte was finally defeated at the Battle of
questions.e: Waterloo in 1815 ended Napoleon's rule. Austerlitz was one of his great victories, and Trafalgar was a naval defeat for France in 1805.

questions.s: In which year did the First World War begin?
questions.e: The war began in 1914 and ended in 1918. 1918 is the year of the armistice, and 1939 is the start of the Second World War.

questions.s: The South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) was founded in
questions.e: Its charter was adopted at the Dhaka summit in December 1985. The secretariat is in Kathmandu.

questions.s: The French Revolution began in which year?
questions.e: The storming of the Bastille in July 1789 marked the start of the revolution. 1815 is the year of Napoleon's defeat at Waterloo.

questions.s: Who led the Bolshevik revolution of 1917 in Russia?
questions.e: Lenin led the Bolshevik party to power. Nicholas II was the Tsar who had abdicated, and Tolstoy was a novelist.

questions.s: NATO, the North Atlantic Treaty Organization, was formed in
questions.e: NATO was founded in April 1949 as a Western defensive alliance. The Soviet-led Warsaw Pact followed in 1955.

questions.s: The Magna Carta, a charter limiting the power of the English king, was sealed in
questions.e: King John agreed to it at Runnymede in 1215. 1066 is the Norman Conquest, much earlier.

questions.s: The Second World War in Europe was triggered by an attack on which country?
questions.e: The German invasion of Poland on 1 September 1939 led Britain and France to declare war. Austria had been annexed in 1938 without a war.

questions.s: OPEC is an organisation of countries that export
questions.e: The Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries was formed in 1960 to coordinate oil policies. It is not concerned with farm products.

questions.s: The great traveller Ibn Battuta was born in
questions.e: Ibn Battuta was from Tangier in Morocco and travelled across much of the Muslim world in the 1300s. Marco Polo was Italian.

questions.s: The Japanese attack on Pearl Harbor brought the USA into the Second World War in
questions.e: The attack came in December 1941. The USA had stayed out of the fighting in the first two years.

questions.s: The Allied landings in Normandy, known as D-Day, took place in
questions.e: On 6 June 1944, Allied forces landed in northern France to open a second front against Germany.

questions.s: The ancient wonder known as the Great Pyramid of Giza was built in
questions.e: It was built as a tomb for Pharaoh Khufu around 2500 BC. The pyramids on the Giza plateau lie near Cairo.

questions.s: Atomic bombs were dropped on which two Japanese cities in 1945?
questions.e: Hiroshima was bombed on 6 August and Nagasaki on 9 August 1945. Tokyo was devastated by conventional firebombing, not an atomic bomb.

questions.s: Under the Abbasid caliphs, the House of Wisdom was a centre of learning in
questions.e: The Abbasids founded Baghdad in 762, and scholars there translated and expanded Greek, Persian and Indian works. Damascus was the Umayyad capital.

questions.s: The Commonwealth of Nations is a group made up mainly of
questions.e: Most of its members were once part of the British Empire, and they cooperate voluntarily. It does not follow the pattern of any defence alliance.

questions.s: The International Criminal Court, which tries individuals for war crimes, sits in
questions.e: The ICC is also at The Hague, but it is different from the International Court of Justice, which settles disputes between states.

questions.s: The Hijri calendar used by Muslims counts from the migration to Madinah, which took place in
questions.e: The Hijrah in 622 CE is year 1 of the Islamic calendar. 570 CE is commonly given as the year of the Holy Prophet's (PBUH) birth.

questions.s: The Panama Canal, joining the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans, opened in
questions.e: The canal opened to ships in August 1914. 1869 is the opening of the Suez Canal.

questions.s: The League of Nations was weakened because it lacked the membership of which major power?
questions.e: The US Senate declined to join, even though President Wilson proposed the League. Britain and France were founding members.

questions.s: The first artificial satellite, Sputnik 1, was launched in
questions.e: The Soviet Union launched it in October 1957 and began the Space Race. Gagarin's flight was in 1961.

questions.s: Malala Yousafzai received the Nobel Peace Prize in which year?
questions.e: She shared the 2014 prize with Kailash Satyarthi for campaigning for children's education, and was then the youngest Nobel laureate. 2012 is the year she was attacked.

questions.s: The Mongol sack of Baghdad in 1258 was led by
questions.e: Hulagu, a grandson of Genghis Khan, destroyed the Abbasid capital. Genghis Khan died in 1227, before the event.

questions.s: The Great Depression is usually said to have begun with the Wall Street crash of
questions.e: The stock market collapsed in October 1929, and unemployment rose across the world. The war years that followed ended the slump.

questions.s: The Battle of Hastings in 1066 led to the conquest of England by
questions.e: William the Conqueror won and became king of England. Harold was the English king who died in the battle.

questions.s: The League of Nations was created after which war?
questions.e: It was set up in 1920 on the proposal of President Wilson to keep peace after 1918. The UN, created after the Second World War, replaced it.

questions.s: Where is the headquarters of the United Nations located?
questions.e: The UN has its main seat in New York City. Geneva hosts many UN offices and agencies but is not the headquarters; it was the home of the old League of Nations.

questions.s: The Congress of Vienna of 1814–15 reorganised Europe after the defeat of
questions.e: European powers met to restore a balance after the Napoleonic Wars. Hitler and Wilhelm II belong to the twentieth century.

questions.s: Who was the first human being to travel into space?
questions.e: The Soviet cosmonaut Gagarin orbited the Earth in April 1961. Shepard was the first American in space a few weeks later, and Armstrong reached the Moon in 1969.

questions.s: How many official languages does the United Nations have?
questions.e: They are Arabic, Chinese, English, French, Russian and Spanish. Two or three are used as working languages in the Secretariat, which can mislead.

questions.s: The Muslim ruler who recaptured Jerusalem from the Crusaders in 1187 was
questions.e: Salahuddin won at the Battle of Hattin and then took the city. Baybars was a Mamluk sultan who fought a century later.

questions.s: The first modern Olympic Games were held in which city in 1896?
questions.e: The Games were revived in Athens, close to the ancient Greek tradition. Pierre de Coubertin led the revival.

questions.s: The Indus Valley Civilisation had major cities at Harappa and
questions.e: Both lie in present-day Pakistan and flourished around 2500 BC. Babylon was in Mesopotamia, and Memphis was in Egypt.

questions.s: The International Labour Organization is headquartered in
questions.e: The ILO, founded in 1919, sets labour standards and is based in Geneva. It later became a UN specialised agency.

questions.s: Which treaty formally ended the First World War with Germany in 1919?
questions.e: The Treaty of Versailles imposed reparations and territorial losses on Germany. Sèvres dealt with the Ottoman Empire, and Vienna belongs to 1815.

questions.s: The Statue of Liberty in New York harbour was a gift from
questions.e: France presented it to the United States in 1886 to mark friendship and the centennial of independence.

questions.s: The Code of Hammurabi, one of the earliest written law codes, comes from
questions.e: King Hammurabi of Babylon, in Mesopotamia, had laws inscribed on a stone pillar around 1750 BC.

questions.s: Who founded the Mongol Empire in the early thirteenth century?
questions.e: Temüjin took the title Genghis Khan in 1206 and united the Mongol tribes. Kublai was his grandson and founded the Yuan dynasty in China.

questions.s: Which disease is caused by a virus?
questions.e: Measles is viral. Typhoid, tuberculosis and cholera are caused by bacteria, so antibiotics help in those.

questions.s: Which organ stores bile?
questions.e: The liver makes bile and the gall bladder stores it for fat digestion.

questions.s: The SI unit of energy is the
questions.e: The joule is energy or work. A watt is energy per second, so it measures power instead.

questions.s: Which gas makes up the largest part of Earth's atmosphere?
questions.e: Nitrogen is about 78 % of dry air, oxygen about 21 %. Oxygen is the gas we need, but it is not the most abundant.

questions.s: A fuse in an electrical circuit is used to
o: break the circuit if current is too high
questions.e: A fuse wire melts when the current is excessive, protecting appliances and preventing fires. It does not store charge, like a capacitor.

questions.s: At sea level, water boils at
questions.e: At normal atmospheric pressure, water boils at 100 °C. At high altitude the boiling point is lower.

questions.s: Which part of the eye controls how much light enters?
questions.e: The iris changes the size of the pupil. The retina is the light-sensitive layer at the back.

questions.s: Which is the only mammal that can truly fly?
questions.e: Bats flap wings supported by long fingers. A flying squirrel only glides, and ostriches and penguins are birds that cannot fly.

questions.s: Which is the largest planet in the solar system?
questions.e: Jupiter is more than 1,000 times Earth's volume. Saturn is second, known for its rings.

questions.s: Which acid is found in a car battery?
questions.e: Lead-acid batteries use sulphuric acid. Citric acid is found in lemons, and acetic acid in vinegar.

questions.s: Which unit is used to measure electrical resistance?
questions.e: The ohm (Ω) measures resistance. The ampere measures current and the volt potential difference.

questions.s: Which gas do plants take in for photosynthesis?
questions.e: Plants combine carbon dioxide and water, using light, to make glucose and release oxygen. They do not take in oxygen for this process.

questions.s: Which is the largest organ of the human body?
questions.e: The skin covers the whole body and weighs more than any internal organ. The liver is the largest internal organ.

questions.s: Which acid is naturally present in the human stomach?
questions.e: Gastric juice contains hydrochloric acid, which kills germs and helps digestion.

questions.s: Which process do green plants use to make their own food?
questions.e: In photosynthesis, plants use light to make glucose from carbon dioxide and water. Transpiration is loss of water vapour from leaves.

questions.s: Which of these is a renewable source of energy?
questions.e: Sunlight is naturally replenished, while coal, gas and petrol take millions of years to form.

questions.s: Which of these is a mammal that lives in water?
questions.e: A dolphin breathes air and feeds its young with milk. Sharks are fish and crocodiles are reptiles.

questions.s: Which is the fastest land animal?
questions.e: A cheetah can reach about 100 km/h in short bursts. Lions are strong but slower.

questions.s: The main cause of acid rain is the release of
questions.e: These gases dissolve in rain to form sulphuric and nitric acids. Oxygen and nitrogen are normal parts of air.

questions.s: Which part of the ear contains the three tiny bones called the hammer, anvil and stirrup?
questions.e: These ossicles pass vibrations from the eardrum to the inner ear. The cochlea in the inner ear turns them into nerve signals.

questions.s: The part of the brain that controls balance and coordination is the
questions.e: The cerebellum coordinates movement and balance. The cerebrum handles thinking and memory.

questions.s: The Moon takes about how long to orbit the Earth?
questions.e: The Moon's orbit takes about 27 days, and the phases repeat every 29.5 days. One year is the Earth's orbit of the Sun.

questions.s: In humans, the number of chromosomes in a normal body cell is
questions.e: Humans have 23 pairs, making 46. Egg and sperm cells carry 23.

questions.s: Deficiency of vitamin C causes
questions.e: Scurvy causes bleeding gums and slow healing. Rickets comes from a lack of vitamin D and night blindness from vitamin A.

questions.s: A solar eclipse happens when the
o: Moon passes between the Sun and the Earth
Earth passes between the Sun and the Moon
questions.e: The Moon blocks sunlight from part of the Earth. When the Earth lies between the Sun and Moon, a lunar eclipse occurs.

questions.s: Who discovered penicillin in 1928?
questions.e: Fleming noticed a mould that killed bacteria on a culture plate. Jenner developed the smallpox vaccine and Pasteur the rabies vaccine.

questions.s: The SI unit of force is the
questions.e: The newton is a kilogram metre per second squared. The joule measures energy.

questions.s: What does the abbreviation 'USB' stand for?
questions.e: USB is a standard connection for peripherals and charging. The other expansions are not real names.

questions.s: Which organ pumps blood around the human body?
questions.e: The heart is a muscular pump that sends blood through arteries and veins. The lungs add oxygen to the blood but do not pump it.

questions.s: Which planet is known as the Red Planet?
questions.e: Iron oxide in the soil gives Mars its reddish colour. Venus is the brightest planet in the sky.

questions.s: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
questions.e: Mercury has the smallest orbit. Venus is hotter because of its thick atmosphere, even though it is farther.

questions.s: Water freezes at what temperature on the Celsius scale?
questions.e: Water freezes at 0 °C, which is 32 °F. At 100 °C it boils at sea level.

questions.s: Which blood group is called the universal donor for red cells?
questions.e: O negative red cells have no A, B or Rh antigens, so almost anyone can receive them. AB positive is the universal recipient.

questions.s: Fossils are most often found in which type of rock?
questions.e: Layers of sediment bury living things gently and preserve them. Igneous rock forms from molten material that would destroy remains.

questions.s: How many planets are there in the solar system?
questions.e: The eight planets are Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune. Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006.

questions.s: The chemical formula of common salt is
questions.e: Table salt is sodium chloride. NaOH is caustic soda, and CaCO₃ is chalk.

questions.s: Light from the Sun takes about how long to reach the Earth?
questions.e: The distance of about 150 million kilometres is covered by light in roughly 8 minutes and 20 seconds.

questions.s: The Sun is a
questions.e: The Sun is a medium-sized star that gives light and heat to the solar system. A planet orbits a star.

questions.s: Anaemia is most commonly caused by a lack of
questions.e: Iron is needed to make haemoglobin in red blood cells. Calcium is needed mainly for bones and teeth.

questions.s: Which type of electromagnetic wave is used to photograph broken bones?
questions.e: X-rays pass through soft tissue but are absorbed by bone, giving an image. Microwaves are used for heating food.

questions.s: Which blood cells carry oxygen?
questions.e: Red cells contain haemoglobin that binds oxygen. White cells fight infection and platelets help clotting.

questions.s: Which galaxy contains our solar system?
questions.e: We live in the Milky Way. Andromeda is the nearest large spiral galaxy to it.

questions.s: Geology is the study of
questions.e: Geologists study rocks, minerals and the structure of the Earth. Plants belong to botany.

questions.s: Which instrument is used to measure atmospheric pressure?
questions.e: A barometer measures air pressure. A hygrometer measures humidity and an anemometer wind speed.

questions.s: Polio mainly affects the
questions.e: The poliovirus can damage nerve cells and cause paralysis. Vaccination prevents the disease.

questions.s: An ammeter is used to measure
questions.e: An ammeter connects in series in a circuit. A voltmeter measures potential difference.

questions.s: Who invented the telephone in 1876?
questions.e: Bell patented the telephone, while Edison is known for the practical light bulb and phonograph. Marconi developed wireless telegraphy.

questions.s: Dengue fever is spread by
questions.e: Aedes bite mainly in the day and breed in clean standing water. Anopheles carry malaria.

questions.s: Which acid is found in vinegar?
questions.e: Vinegar contains about 5 % acetic acid. Lactic acid is found in sour milk.

questions.s: A tadpole is the young stage of a
questions.e: Frogs are amphibians, and tadpoles develop gills first and lungs later. Many people mistake them for fish.

questions.s: The first successful general-purpose electronic digital computers appeared in which decade?
questions.e: Machines such as ENIAC were built in the 1940s. Charles Babbage designed a mechanical computer in the 1800s but it was not completed.

questions.s: Which planet has the most prominent system of rings?
questions.e: Saturn's bright rings are made of ice and rock particles. Jupiter, Uranus and Neptune have faint rings.

questions.s: Which vitamin is produced in the skin by sunlight?
questions.e: Ultraviolet light helps the skin make vitamin D, which is needed for strong bones. Vitamin C comes from fruit and vegetables.

questions.s: Who proposed the law of universal gravitation?
questions.e: Newton explained that every mass attracts every other mass. Einstein later gave a deeper theory, general relativity.

questions.s: The device used to store electric charge is a
questions.e: A capacitor holds charge on two plates. A resistor limits current.

questions.s: The speed of light is approximately
questions.e: Light travels about 300,000 kilometres each second in a vacuum, and much faster than sound.

questions.s: Which vitamin is needed by the body for normal blood clotting?
questions.e: Vitamin K helps the liver make clotting factors, so a lack of it can cause prolonged bleeding. Vitamin A is needed for vision.

questions.s: Which is the largest animal living on Earth today?
questions.e: The blue whale can exceed 25 metres in length. The African elephant is the largest land animal.

questions.s: Which device is used to convert alternating current to direct current?
questions.e: A rectifier uses diodes to allow current in one direction. A transformer only changes the voltage of alternating current.

questions.s: The World Wide Web was invented by
questions.e: Berners-Lee proposed it at CERN in 1989. The web is a service running on the internet, which is a different network.

questions.s: Which is the hardest natural substance?
questions.e: Diamond is a form of carbon and has the highest hardness on the Mohs scale. Steel is a man-made alloy.

questions.s: Lack of iodine in the diet causes
questions.e: The thyroid gland needs iodine to make hormones and swells without it. Anaemia is usually due to a lack of iron.

questions.s: Which pigment gives leaves their green colour?
questions.e: Chlorophyll absorbs red and blue light and reflects green. Melanin is the pigment in human skin, and haemoglobin colours blood.

questions.s: Which part of a computer is called its 'brain'?
questions.e: The central processing unit carries out instructions. A hard disk is only used for long-term storage.

questions.s: Spiders belong to which group of animals?
questions.e: Spiders have eight legs and two body parts, unlike insects, which have six legs and three body parts.

questions.s: Who is credited with developing the practical incandescent light bulb in 1879?
questions.e: Edison's team made a long-lasting carbon-filament bulb. Faraday worked on electromagnetism and Watt on the steam engine.

questions.s: Which colour of visible light has the longest wavelength?
questions.e: Red has the longest wavelength and violet the shortest in the visible spectrum.

questions.s: How many bones are there in an adult human body?
questions.e: An adult skeleton has 206 bones. Babies have more, because some bones fuse as they grow.

questions.s: Which device converts sound into electrical signals?
questions.e: A microphone converts sound to electrical signals, and a loudspeaker does the opposite.

questions.s: Which disease is spread by the Anopheles mosquito?
questions.e: Malaria is caused by the Plasmodium parasite, which is spread by female Anopheles mosquitoes. Cholera, typhoid and tuberculosis are bacterial diseases spread in other ways.

questions.s: Which gas is used to fill party balloons so that they float?
questions.e: Helium is lighter than air and non-flammable. Hydrogen is also light, but it burns easily.

questions.s: What is the normal body temperature of a healthy person in degrees Celsius?
questions.e: Normal body temperature is about 37 °C, or 98.6 °F. Values far from this signal illness or danger.

questions.s: Which gas do humans breathe out in larger amounts than they breathe in?
questions.e: Cells produce carbon dioxide during respiration and the lungs remove it. Nitrogen is breathed in and out almost unchanged.

questions.s: Insulin, which controls blood sugar, is produced by the
questions.e: Special cells in the pancreas make insulin. Lack of it causes diabetes mellitus.

questions.s: Which organ of the human body filters waste from the blood to make urine?
questions.e: Each kidney contains about a million nephrons that filter blood. The liver processes nutrients and toxins, but urine is formed in the kidneys.

questions.s: Which gas is mainly responsible for the greenhouse effect caused by burning fossil fuels?
questions.e: Carbon dioxide traps heat in the atmosphere. Helium and neon are inert and play no such role.

questions.s: Which metal is liquid at room temperature?
questions.e: Mercury melts at about −39 °C. Most other metals are solid at room temperature.

questions.s: Who developed the first successful smallpox vaccine?
questions.e: Jenner used cowpox material in 1796 to protect against smallpox. Pasteur came later and worked on rabies and anthrax.

questions.s: Sound cannot travel through
questions.e: Sound needs a material medium to travel, so it cannot pass through empty space. It moves faster in solids and liquids than in air.

questions.s: Which instrument records the ground vibrations of earthquakes?
questions.e: A seismograph records ground motion and shows their strength. An altimeter measures height.

questions.s: Which layer of the atmosphere protects living things from most ultraviolet rays?
questions.e: Ozone in the stratosphere absorbs harmful UV radiation. Weather happens in the troposphere, the lowest layer.

questions.s: The blood vessels that carry blood away from the heart are called
questions.e: Arteries carry blood away from the heart. Veins return blood to it, and capillaries are tiny vessels where exchange occurs.

questions.s: Mount Fuji is a well-known volcano in
questions.e: Mount Fuji is Japan's highest mountain, at about 3,776 m. Indonesia and the Philippines have other well-known volcanoes.

questions.s: What is the capital of Peru?
questions.e: Lima is the capital. Cusco was the Inca capital.

questions.s: London stands on which river?
questions.e: The Thames flows through London to the North Sea. The Seine passes through Paris.

questions.s: The Thar Desert is shared by Pakistan and
questions.e: The Thar covers parts of Sindh and Rajasthan. It lies mainly in the east of Pakistan.

questions.s: The Great Wall is a famous monument in which country?
questions.e: The Great Wall was built over many centuries to guard the northern frontier of China.

questions.s: What is the capital of the United States?
questions.e: Washington, D.C. is the seat of the federal government. New York is the largest city.

questions.s: What is the capital of New Zealand?
questions.e: Wellington is the capital. Auckland is the largest city.

questions.s: Which is the largest lake in the world by area?
questions.e: The Caspian Sea is the biggest inland water body, though it is salty. Lake Superior is the largest freshwater lake by area.

questions.s: What is the capital of Nepal?
questions.e: Kathmandu lies in a valley in the Himalaya. Thimphu is the capital of Bhutan.

questions.s: What is the capital of Turkey?
questions.e: Ankara became the capital in 1923. Istanbul is the largest city and was the Ottoman capital.

questions.s: Which is the largest hot desert in the world?
questions.e: The Sahara covers much of North Africa. The Gobi is a cold desert in Asia.

questions.s: Which is the largest continent by area?
questions.e: Asia covers about a third of the world's land area. Africa is second.

questions.s: What is the capital of Argentina?
questions.e: Buenos Aires is the capital on the Río de la Plata. Santiago is Chile's capital.

questions.s: What is the capital of Switzerland?
questions.e: Bern is the federal city. Zurich is the largest city and Geneva hosts many organisations.

questions.s: The Strait of Gibraltar separates Spain from
questions.e: It joins the Atlantic Ocean with the Mediterranean Sea, and at its narrowest the two continents are about 14 km apart.

questions.s: What is the capital of China?
questions.e: Beijing is the capital. Shanghai is the largest city by population.

questions.s: The Eiffel Tower is a famous landmark of which city?
questions.e: The tower stands on the Champ de Mars in Paris. Many guess other European capitals.

questions.s: The world's smallest country by area is
questions.e: Vatican City is about 0.44 km². Monaco is the second smallest.

questions.s: The Bosphorus Strait separates the European and Asian parts of
questions.e: It connects the Black Sea with the Sea of Marmara, and the city of Istanbul lies on both sides.

questions.s: The imaginary line at 0° latitude is called the
questions.e: The equator divides the Earth into northern and southern hemispheres. The Prime Meridian is a line of longitude.

questions.s: Niagara Falls is on the border of the United States and
questions.e: The falls lie between New York State and Ontario, on the Niagara River.

questions.s: The Panama Canal connects the Atlantic Ocean with the
questions.e: It cuts through Panama, saving ships a long voyage around South America.

questions.s: What is the capital of Morocco?
questions.e: Rabat is the capital. Casablanca is the largest city and an economic centre.

questions.s: What is the capital of Japan?
questions.e: Tokyo has been the capital since 1868. Kyoto was the earlier imperial capital.

questions.s: The Ganges (Ganga) river flows mainly through
questions.e: The Ganges rises in the Himalaya and crosses northern India, ending in Bangladesh. The Indus is the main river of Pakistan.

questions.s: What is the capital of Iran?
questions.e: Tehran is the capital. Mashhad is an important religious city.

questions.s: The Ural Mountains form part of the boundary between
questions.e: They run north to south in Russia. They are the traditional dividing line of the two continents.

questions.s: What is the capital of Kenya?
questions.e: Nairobi is the capital and largest city. Kampala is the capital of Uganda.

questions.s: The rock-cut city of Petra is in
questions.e: Petra was the capital of the Nabataeans and lies in southern Jordan.

questions.s: What is the capital of Bangladesh?
questions.e: Dhaka is the capital and largest city. Chittagong is the main port.

questions.s: The Great Barrier Reef, the largest coral reef system, is off the coast of
questions.e: It runs along the north-east coast of Queensland, Australia.

questions.s: What is the capital of Saudi Arabia?
questions.e: Riyadh is the capital. Jeddah is a major port, and Makkah and Madinah are holy cities.

questions.s: What is the currency of Turkey?
questions.e: Turkey uses the lira. It is not in the eurozone.

questions.s: Angkor Wat, a huge temple complex, is located in
questions.e: Angkor Wat was built by the Khmer Empire in the twelfth century. It is Cambodia's best-known site.

questions.s: What is the currency of China?
questions.e: The Chinese currency is called the renminbi, and its unit is the yuan. The yen is Japanese.

questions.s: The Tropic of Cancer lies at about
questions.e: It marks the northernmost latitude where the Sun can be directly overhead. 23½° S is the Tropic of Capricorn.

questions.s: The Atacama Desert, one of the driest places on Earth, is in
questions.e: It lies along the Pacific coast of northern Chile. Rain may not fall for years in some parts.

questions.s: Which is the smallest continent by area?
questions.e: Australia is the smallest continent. Europe is larger, and Antarctica is much larger though uninhabited.

questions.s: Mount Kilimanjaro, the highest mountain in Africa, is in
questions.e: It lies in northern Tanzania, near the Kenyan border. Mount Kenya is a different mountain.

questions.s: The Strait of Hormuz links the Persian Gulf with the
questions.e: It lies between Iran and Oman. The Gulf of Oman opens to the Arabian Sea.

questions.s: What is the capital of Australia?
questions.e: Canberra was built as a compromise between Sydney and Melbourne. Sydney is the largest city but not the capital.

questions.s: What is the currency of the United Arab Emirates?
questions.e: The UAE uses the dirham. Riyal is the name used in Saudi Arabia, Qatar and others.

questions.s: The Andes mountain range runs along the western side of
questions.e: It is the longest continental range, running through several countries. The Rockies lie in North America.

questions.s: The Suez Canal connects the Mediterranean Sea with the
questions.e: It runs across Egypt, so ships need not sail around Africa.

questions.s: What is the capital of Canada?
questions.e: Ottawa is the capital. Toronto is the largest city.

questions.s: The Amazon River flows mainly through which country?
questions.e: Most of the Amazon basin is in Brazil, though the river begins in the Andes in Peru. It flows into the Atlantic.

questions.s: The Prime Meridian, 0° longitude, passes through
questions.e: The Greenwich Observatory was chosen in 1884 as the zero point. The equator is a different line.

questions.s: Which river flows through Egypt and the city of Cairo?
questions.e: The Nile flows north into the Mediterranean Sea. The Congo is in central Africa.

questions.s: The Danube, a major European river, flows into the
questions.e: It rises in Germany and flows eastwards through several capitals. The Rhine flows to the North Sea.

questions.s: Which is the highest mountain peak above sea level in the world?
questions.e: Everest, on the Nepal–China border, is about 8,849 m high. K2, on the Pakistan–China border, is the second highest.

questions.s: Russia is the largest country in the world by
questions.e: It spans eleven time zones. Population is larger in China and India.

questions.s: What is the currency of Saudi Arabia?
questions.e: The Saudi riyal is the currency. The dirham is used in the UAE.

questions.s: The deepest freshwater lake in the world is
questions.e: Lake Baikal in Siberia is more than 1,600 m deep. Lake Titicaca is high in the Andes.

questions.s: What is the capital of Mongolia?
questions.e: Ulaanbaatar is the capital. The other cities serve different countries.

questions.s: What is the currency of India?
questions.e: India's currency is the rupee. The taka is used in Bangladesh and the rupiah in Indonesia.

questions.s: Which is the smallest ocean in the world?
questions.e: The Arctic Ocean is the smallest and shallowest. It lies mostly around the North Pole.

questions.s: What is the capital of Brazil?
questions.e: Brasília was built in the 1950s and became the capital in 1960. Rio was the earlier capital.

questions.s: What is the currency of Russia?
questions.e: Russia uses the rouble. The zloty is the currency of Poland and the hryvnia of Ukraine.

questions.s: What is the capital of Uruguay?
questions.e: Montevideo is the capital of Uruguay. Santiago is the capital of Chile, Asunción of Paraguay, and La Paz is a seat of government in Bolivia.

questions.s: The deepest known point of the oceans is in the
questions.e: The Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench of the Pacific is about 11 km deep. The Puerto Rico Trench is the deepest part of the Atlantic.

questions.s: Which is the second highest mountain in the world?
questions.e: K2 lies in the Karakoram on the Pakistan–China border. Nanga Parbat is lower, at about 8,126 m.

questions.s: Which is the largest ocean in the world?
questions.e: The Pacific covers more area than all the land on Earth. The Atlantic is second.

questions.s: Into which sea does the River Nile empty?
questions.e: It drains northwards through a delta. The Red Sea lies east of Egypt.

questions.s: The Kaaba is in which city?
questions.e: The Kaaba lies in the Masjid al-Haram in Makkah. Madinah has the Prophet's mosque.

questions.s: The Yangtze, the longest river in Asia, flows through
questions.e: The Yangtze flows from the Tibetan plateau to the East China Sea. It is the longest river of Asia and the third longest in the world.

questions.s: What is the currency of South Africa?
questions.e: The South African rand is the national currency. The naira is the currency of Nigeria.

questions.s: The Colosseum is a famous ancient arena in which city?
questions.e: The Colosseum is in Rome, Italy. The Parthenon is in Athens.

questions.s: Which two rivers form the Mesopotamian plain in modern Iraq?
questions.e: Mesopotamia means land between the rivers, and the plain lies between the Tigris and the Euphrates.

questions.s: What is the currency of the United Kingdom?
questions.e: The UK uses the pound sterling. It has not adopted the euro.

questions.s: Which ocean lies to the south of Pakistan?
questions.e: Pakistan's coast along Sindh and Balochistan is on the Arabian Sea, which is part of the Indian Ocean.

questions.s: What is the capital of Nigeria?
questions.e: Abuja became the capital in 1991. Lagos is the largest city and was the earlier capital.

questions.s: The Gobi Desert lies between
questions.e: The Gobi is a large cold desert across northern China and southern Mongolia. The Sahara is the desert of North Africa.

questions.s: The Arabian Peninsula is bordered on the west by the
questions.e: It lies between the Red Sea and the Persian Gulf, with the Arabian Sea to the south-east.

questions.s: The Victoria Falls lie on the border of
questions.e: The Zambezi River plunges over the falls between Zambia and Zimbabwe.

questions.s: What is the capital of the United Arab Emirates?
questions.e: Abu Dhabi is the capital. Dubai is the best-known commercial city.

questions.s: How many continents are there in the world, by the usual count?
questions.e: The seven continents are Asia, Africa, North America, South America, Antarctica, Europe and Australia (Oceania). Some models combine them, which is why other numbers are heard.

questions.s: Lake Victoria is the largest lake in
questions.e: Uganda, Kenya and Tanzania share it. It is the source of the White Nile.

questions.s: Which river flows through Baghdad?
questions.e: Baghdad is on the Tigris. The Euphrates flows to its west.

questions.s: What is the capital of Afghanistan?
questions.e: Kabul has been the capital for a long time. Kandahar is a city in the south.

questions.s: What is the currency of Japan?
questions.e: Japan uses the yen. The won is South Korean and the yuan is Chinese.

questions.s: The Himalayas form the northern boundary of which region?
questions.e: They form a high barrier between the Indian subcontinent and the Tibetan plateau.

questions.s: The ancient Inca city of Machu Picchu is in
questions.e: It lies high in the Andes of Peru. Mexico's ancient cities were Mayan or Aztec.

questions.s: What does NADRA stand for?
o: National Department of Registration and Assessment
questions.e: NADRA issues the CNIC and maintains the national citizen register.

questions.s: The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) has its headquarters in
questions.e: The IAEA promotes peaceful use of nuclear energy and is based in Vienna.

questions.s: Fiscal policy of a government concerns
questions.e: Taxes and government spending are fiscal tools, whereas interest rates and the money supply are monetary tools of the central bank.

questions.s: The two houses of Pakistan's Parliament are the National Assembly and the
questions.e: The Senate gives equal representation to each province. Provincial assemblies are separate bodies.

questions.s: What does WAPDA stand for?
o: Water Authority of Pakistan Development Agency
questions.e: WAPDA was set up in 1958 to develop water and power resources in Pakistan.

questions.s: An exchange of goods without using money is called
questions.e: In barter, one good is swapped for another, which needs a double coincidence of wants. Money removes the problem.

questions.s: The European Union uses a common currency called the
questions.e: Many but not all EU members use the euro. The pound remains the British currency.

questions.s: Which international organisation is responsible for civil aviation standards and has its headquarters in Montreal?
questions.e: The International Civil Aviation Organization is a UN agency. The IAEA is in Vienna.

questions.s: What does SAARC stand for?
o: Southern Asian Alliance for Rural Cooperation
South Asian Agency for Regional Commerce
Southeast Asian Association for Regional Cooperation
South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation
questions.e: SAARC promotes regional cooperation in South Asia. Southeast Asia has ASEAN instead.

questions.s: Which institution is the central bank of Pakistan?
questions.e: The SBP issues currency and sets monetary policy. The NBP is a commercial bank owned by the state, and the FBR collects taxes.

questions.s: What does FIFA stand for?
questions.e: FIFA is the world governing body of football, founded in Paris in 1904.

questions.s: Which organ of government carries out the laws?
questions.e: The executive includes the president, prime minister, cabinet and civil servants who run the state.

questions.s: What does UNESCO stand for?
o: United Nations Economic and Social Council
United Nations Education and Safety Committee
United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization
Union of National Educational Societies and Colleges
questions.e: UNESCO promotes education, science and culture and protects heritage sites. ECOSOC is a different UN body.

questions.s: The body that conducts general elections in Pakistan is the
questions.e: The Election Commission is an independent constitutional body. The FPSC recruits civil servants.

questions.s: The idea of separation of powers among three organs of government is associated with
questions.e: Montesquieu argued in The Spirit of the Laws that power should be divided to prevent tyranny. Rousseau wrote on the social contract.

questions.s: In Pakistan, who is the head of state?
questions.e: The President is the constitutional head of state, while the Prime Minister heads the government. The post of Governor-General ended in 1956.

questions.s: Opportunity cost is best described as
o: the money paid for a purchase
the cost of making one extra unit
the value of the next best alternative given up
questions.e: Choosing one thing means giving up another, and that lost option is the cost. The money paid is simply the price.

questions.s: What does NATO stand for?
questions.e: NATO is a military alliance of North American and European countries. It is not a trade body.

questions.s: Wages are the reward for which factor of production?
questions.e: Labour earns wages, land earns rent, capital earns interest and enterprise earns profit.

questions.s: What does FBR stand for?
questions.e: The FBR is the federal tax collecting body of Pakistan.

questions.s: Which of these is NOT a function of money?
questions.e: Money helps exchange, saves value and measures prices. It does not produce goods; people and capital do.

questions.s: The financial (fiscal) year of the government of Pakistan runs from
questions.e: Pakistan uses a July–June fiscal year, and the budget is presented in June. India uses April–March.

questions.s: Which of these is a direct tax?
questions.e: Direct taxes are paid by the person they are levied on. Sales tax is passed on to consumers through prices, so it is indirect.

questions.s: In a federation, power is
o: divided between the centre and units
questions.e: Federal states like Pakistan share powers between the federal government and provinces. A unitary state keeps them at the centre.

questions.s: A two-house legislature is called
questions.e: Bicameral means two chambers. Pakistan's Parliament has the National Assembly and the Senate.

questions.s: What does CNIC stand for?
questions.e: The CNIC is the standard identity document for Pakistani adults.

questions.s: Which of these is a factor of production?
questions.e: Land, labour, capital and enterprise produce goods. Profit and rent are rewards, not inputs.

questions.s: What does IMF stand for?
questions.e: The IMF lends to countries with balance of payments trouble and promotes monetary cooperation.

questions.s: The minimum age for a citizen to cast a vote in Pakistan is
questions.e: An adult citizen who is 18 and registered can vote. The age of 25 is the minimum to contest a National Assembly seat.

questions.s: Dividing a country's total income by its population gives
questions.e: Per capita income shows average income per person. It does not show how it is shared.

questions.s: The total of goods and services produced by a country's citizens, whether at home or abroad, is called
questions.e: GNP includes income earned by nationals abroad. GDP counts only production inside the country's borders.

questions.s: Goods sold by a country to other countries are called
questions.e: Exports earn foreign exchange. Imports are goods bought from other countries.

questions.s: What does FAO stand for?
questions.e: The FAO leads international efforts to defeat hunger and improve farming.

questions.s: What does UNHCR stand for?
o: United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees
questions.e: The UNHCR protects refugees and is headquartered in Geneva.

questions.s: A sustained fall in a country's total output over several months is called a
questions.e: A recession shows as falling GDP and rising unemployment. A boom is the opposite.

questions.s: A system in which the prime minister and cabinet are answerable to the legislature is called
questions.e: In a parliamentary system the cabinet needs the confidence of the house. In a presidential system, the president is independent of the legislature.

questions.s: A general and continuing rise in the prices of goods and services is called
questions.e: Inflation lowers what each rupee can buy. Deflation is the opposite, a fall in the general price level.

questions.s: If a country's imports exceed its exports, it has a
questions.e: The gap in goods and services is a trade deficit. A surplus occurs when exports exceed imports.

questions.s: The State Bank of Pakistan began functioning in
questions.e: The bank was formally opened by Quaid-e-Azam in July 1948. Before it, the Reserve Bank of India handled these tasks.

questions.s: What does CPEC stand for?
questions.e: CPEC is a collection of infrastructure projects linking western China with the Pakistani port of Gwadar.

questions.s: According to the law of demand, when the price of a good rises, the quantity demanded usually
questions.e: Buyers purchase less at a higher price, other things being equal. The relationship is inverse.

questions.s: According to the law of supply, when the price of a good rises, the quantity supplied usually
questions.e: Producers are willing to sell more at higher prices because profit rises. Supply and price move in the same direction.

questions.s: In Pakistan, the Senate gives each province
questions.e: Each province has the same number of Senate seats, which protects smaller provinces. The National Assembly seats are based on population.

questions.s: What does GDP stand for in economics?
questions.e: GDP is the total value of goods and services produced inside a country in a year. It measures output, not the government's debt.

questions.s: What does OIC stand for?
questions.e: The OIC is the collective voice of Muslim-majority states. It was founded in 1969.

questions.s: The main purpose of a government budget is to
questions.e: The budget lists expected income, mostly from taxes, and planned spending. The central bank handles currency and rates.

questions.s: What does OPEC stand for?
o: Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries
Organization of Power and Energy Companies
questions.e: OPEC coordinates oil policies among its members. It was founded in Baghdad in 1960.

questions.s: The Constitution of a country is
questions.e: A constitution sets out the structure of the state and the rights of its citizens. All other laws must follow it.

questions.s: What does ECO stand for in international affairs?
questions.e: ECO links Pakistan, Iran, Turkey and several Central Asian states. It is a regional economic body.

questions.s: What does WHO stand for?
questions.e: The WHO is a UN agency for international public health. The other expansions are not real.

questions.s: What does ICC stand for in cricket?
questions.e: The ICC governs international cricket and organises world tournaments.

questions.s: Which organ of government interprets the laws and settles disputes?
questions.e: Courts apply and interpret the law. Parliament makes it and the cabinet implements it.

questions.s: A vote of the people on a single public question is called a
questions.e: A referendum asks citizens to accept or reject one proposal. A by-election fills one vacant seat.

questions.s: A general fall in the price level of goods and services is called
questions.e: Deflation is a sustained fall in prices. Depreciation refers to a fall in the value of a currency or asset.

questions.s: A government in which a few rule in their own interest, often through wealth, is called
questions.e: An oligarchy is rule by a small group. A democracy is rule by the people.

questions.s: What does WTO stand for?
questions.e: The WTO oversees rules of international trade. The other options are not real organisations.

questions.s: What does UNICEF stand for?
questions.e: It was first named the International Children's Emergency Fund, and the old initials remained in use.

questions.s: The lower house of the Parliament of Pakistan is the
questions.e: Parliament has two houses: the National Assembly is the lower house and the Senate is the upper house. Provincial assemblies are not part of Parliament.

questions.s: The price at which the quantity demanded equals the quantity supplied is called the
questions.e: At this price, the market clears. Above it there is surplus, and below it shortage.

questions.s: Which of these is an indirect tax?
questions.e: An indirect tax is collected from sellers and passed on to buyers. Income tax is levied directly on earnings.

questions.s: Monetary policy is mainly controlled by the
questions.e: The central bank adjusts interest rates and the money supply. Parliament passes the budget.

questions.s: A form of government in which the head of state is an elected president and the state is not ruled by a king is a
questions.e: In a republic, power rests with the people and their representatives. A monarchy is led by a hereditary ruler.

questions.s: A market with only one seller and no close substitutes is called a
questions.e: A monopolist can control the price. Oligopoly means a few sellers.

questions.s: The African Union has its headquarters in
questions.e: The AU is based in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.

questions.s: What does NAB stand for in Pakistan?
questions.e: NAB deals with corruption cases. The Auditor General's office does the government's audit.

questions.s: A budget in which government expenditure exceeds revenue shows a
questions.e: The gap must be financed by borrowing or by printing money. A surplus is the opposite.

questions.s: Interest is the reward for which factor of production?
questions.e: Capital earns interest. Land earns rent, so rent is a common wrong guess.

questions.s: Which organ of government makes laws?
questions.e: The legislature, Parliament in Pakistan, makes laws. The executive carries them out and the judiciary interprets them.

questions.s: Interpol is an organisation that helps in
questions.e: Interpol links national police forces to fight cross-border crime. It has no police of its own to arrest people in other countries.

questions.s: A tax levied on goods when they enter a country is called a
questions.e: Customs duty is paid on imports at the border. Excise duty is charged on goods made inside the country.

questions.s: What does FIA stand for in Pakistan?
questions.e: The FIA is a federal agency that investigates matters like cybercrime and human trafficking.

questions.s: What does HEC stand for in Pakistan?
questions.e: The HEC regulates and funds universities. It replaced the University Grants Commission in 2002.
